Subject: Dedicated deployment — data sequestration, snapshots, and deletion proof (FinHoldings)

Rafael,

Thanks for taking this. We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a regulated storage indexing workflow and have a few specific asks around data locality and end-of-life destruction:

- Can you confirm whether production data and any persistent snapshots/backups can be strictly sequestered to a single AWS region (us-west-2) with no cross-region replication by default?
- For backups/snapshots: are they stored in the same region by default and encrypted with customer-managed keys (CMK)? If so, can you provide the key lifecycle and rotation policy we can reference for audit?
- Deletion: when we request a data erasure for a tenant, what is the exact sequence (logical delete, snapshot purge, overwrite, cryptographic key retirement)? What artifacts do you provide as proof of deletion (job id, timestamp, SHA256 receipt, audit log export)?
- Can you provide expected timelines (worst-case) for complete removal from live and backup tiers? We need something we can present to our compliance team.

Attached is a short questionnaire from our security team. Appreciate an initial answer and then any evidence or runbook you can share.

Paul

Paul —

Thanks for the clear list. High-level answers up front, then I'll loop in our security lead for the technical receipts and runbook.

- Region pinning: Redwood Dedicated supports strict data-plane region pinning. By default, data nodes (and their persistent volumes/snapshots) stay within the customer-selected region (us-west-2). The control plane (orchestration and billing) is global but contains only metadata; plaintext/PHI is never stored outside the pinned region unless the customer explicitly enables cross-region DR.

- Snapshots/backups: snapshots are stored encrypted at rest using a CMK. For Dedicated we can accept a customer-managed key (KMS) or use a Redwood-managed key scoped to the region. Cross-region snapshot replication is OFF by default for region-pinned deployments; replication only occurs when DR is enabled in the contract.

- Deletion lifecycle: standard sequence is (1) logical delete and access revocation, (2) background data purge job that removes objects and marks storage blocks for reclamation, (3) snapshot lifecycle triggers retention deletion per policy, and (4) cryptographic key retirement for CMKs where applicable. We can provide a signed deletion receipt that includes job id, timestamps, and an audit log excerpt. For additional assurance we offer a certified overwrite schedule for physical media where applicable via our hosting partners.

- Timelines: typical logical purge visible within 24 hours; background purge and block reclamation completed in 24–72 hours for active data. Snapshot retention deletion (if a snapshot existed) depends on retention window; with a 90-day default snapshot retention the backup deletion path may take up to 90 days unless you request immediate destruction and we engage the emergency purge process (estimated 7–30 days depending on cloud provider media lifecycle). We can provide contract amendments to shorten snapshot retention to meet your policy.

I'm looping in Karthik (security) and Marissa (solutions) to provide the concrete artifacts (runbook, example deletion receipt, and KMS key lifecycle doc).

Best,
Rafael

Paul / team —

Following up with the technical detail and the artifacts you requested. Summary bullets follow and I've attached a condensed runbook excerpt to this thread.

- Data-plane placement: we provision tenant volumes and stateful nodes only in the contracted region (us-west-2). The storage layer uses regional block storage and S3-compatible object stores tied to that region. Network ACLs, VPC peering, and host tenancy controls are enforced so that control-plane services do not have access to raw customer payloads.

- Snapshot lifecycle and encryption: snapshots are AES-256 encrypted with CMKs. Customers may supply an AWS KMS CMK ARN for the region; if using a Redwood-managed CMK we rotate keys on a 90-day schedule with a documented rotation policy. Snapshots are immutable objects; deletion triggers a lifecycle job that marks them for removal and instructs the cloud provider to delete associated object manifests.

- Deletion proof we can provide: signed deletion receipts that include the deletion_job_id, initiating_user, tenant_id, object_manifests_deleted (list), snapshot_ids (if applicable), and a SHA256 digest over the audit excerpt. We produce the receipt as a digitally-signed PDF and export the audit lines in CSV for your auditors. Example receipt fields are in the attached runbook excerpt.

- RPO/RTO and timelines:
  - Logical revocation and tenant access cutoff: immediate (within seconds).
  - Live-data purge and block reclamation: target 24–72 hours, worst-case 7 days in overloaded maintenance windows.
  - Backup/snapshot purge without contract amendment: subject to retention window (default 90 days).
  - Emergency snapshot destruction (contract amendment): target 7–30 days depending on cloud provider deletion propagation and media overwrite policies.

- Evidence chain: we maintain immutable audit logs (append-only) with SHA256 chain hashes per day. For compliance deliveries we can produce a hashed export, signed by Redwood's KMS, and a certificate of destruction from the cloud provider when available.

Question for FinHoldings: do you need the CMK to be customer-supplied (preferred for highest assurance) or is a Redwood-managed CMK acceptable with rotation and rotation-history evidence? If customer-supplied we will require ARNs and operator contact details so we can bake key usage into the provisioning template.

Related internal ticket: https://redwood.internal/secure/DR-7092 (contains sample receipts and previous customer examples).

If you're happy with the timelines above, Rafael — do we want to offer a negotiated 30-day snapshot retention for FH as a deal term? Marissa, can you confirm operational impact and pricing delta?

Thanks,
Karthik
